      - term: United Kingdom
      - definition:
        - text: In the UK (MHRA, September 2026), Ozempic is licensed for diabetes and Mounjaro for diabetes and weight. Wegovy is licensed for weight management and cardiovascular risk reduction; MHRA added weight management to Mounjaro in November 2023. MHRA says retatrutide is not authorised in the UK and anyone selling it does so illegally (24 July 2026), and in May 2026 it made its largest seizure of unlicensed weight-loss medicines.
        - generic: "Source: Ozempic 1 mg solution for injection in pre-filled pen — Summary of Product Characteristics (UK) · Wegovy 2.4 mg FlexTouch solution for injection in pre-filled pen — Summary of Product Characteristics (UK) · Mounjaro KwikPen 5 mg solution for injection in pre-filled pen — Summary of Product Characteristics (UK) · MHRA authorises diabetes drug Mounjaro (tirzepatide) for weight management and weight loss (press release) · No summer shortcut for safe weight loss (press release) · Two arrested during the MHRA's largest ever seizure of unlicensed weight loss medicines (press release)"
      - term: European Union
      - definition:
        - text: In the EU, semaglutide is authorised as Ozempic for diabetes (since 8 February 2018) and Wegovy for weight management (since 6 January 2022), and tirzepatide as Mounjaro for diabetes and adult weight management (since 15 September 2022), all prescription-only. In June 2024 EMA and HMA's shortage steering group said GLP-1 receptor agonists are not approved for, and should not be used for, cosmetic weight loss, and on 3 September 2025 EMA and HMA warned of a sharp rise in illegal medicines sold online and on social media as semaglutide, liraglutide or tirzepatide, which are unauthorised and may not contain the stated substance.
        - generic: "Source: EU actions to tackle shortages of GLP-1 receptor agonists (news) · Ozempic (semaglutide) — EPAR medicine overview · Wegovy (semaglutide) — EPAR medicine overview · Mounjaro (tirzepatide) — EPAR medicine overview · Union Register of medicinal products for human use (authorised, not active and refused lists) · Download medicine data — EMA medicines data table (centrally authorised, refused, withdrawn and withdrawn-application medicines) · Warning about sharp rise in illegal medicines sold in the EU (news)"
      - term: Portugal
      - definition:
        - text: In Portugal, Wegovy and Mounjaro are authorised through the EU centralised procedure and are prescription-only, and on 4 July 2024 INFARMED stated that Ozempic, Trulicity and Victoza must not be prescribed to patients who are not diabetic (Circular 045/CD/100.20.200). In September 2025 INFARMED relayed the EMA and HMA warning of a sharp increase in the illegal marketing of medicines presented as GLP-1 receptor agonists, and stated that in Portugal medicines can only be bought on the internet from the websites of pharmacies and licensed non-prescription medicine outlets (LVMNSRM).
        - generic: "Source: Infomed – base de dados de medicamentos do Infarmed (pesquisa avançada and 'Detalhes do Medicamento' pages) · Infomed – Guia e condições de utilização · Circular Informativa N.º 045/CD/100.20.200 – Recomendações para gestão da disponibilidade dos medicamentos agonistas do recetor da GLP-1 · EMA e HMA alertam para aumento da venda de medicamentos ilegais comercializados como análogos do GLP-1"
      - term: Brazil
      - definition:
        - text: In Brazil, as of September 2026, Ozempic is indicated for adults with insufficiently controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus, Wegovy is indicated for weight management in adults, Mounjaro is indicated for chronic weight management in adults, and the approved synthetic semaglutide copies are indicated for adult patients with insufficiently controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus. Nota Técnica 200/2025 (August 2025) permits compounding of chemically synthesised APIs provided registered medicines with the same molecule already exist in Brazil, and ANVISA inspections from January to April 2026 led to the closure of 8 of the 26 establishments assessed and the seizure of more than 1.3 million units of irregular injectable medicines.
        - generic: "Source: Ozempic (semaglutida) – bula profissional · Dados abertos de medicamentos registrados (DADOS_ABERTOS_MEDICAMENTOS.csv) · Wegovy (semaglutida) – bula profissional · Mounjaro (tirzepatida) – bula profissional · Consultas – Medicamentos (product and substance search) · Anvisa aprova primeira caneta de semaglutida sintética análoga ao Ozempic para diabetes · Anvisa registra cinco novas canetas de semaglutida · Anvisa esclarece e determina regras para manipulação de canetas de GLP-1 · Nota Técnica nº 200/2025/SEI/GIMED/GGFIS/DIRE4/ANVISA – importação, manipulação e controle sanitário de IFAs agonistas GLP-1 · Anvisa e Polícia Federal farão análise conjunta de canetas irregulares apreendidas · Anvisa anuncia novas medidas de combate a irregularidades na importação e manipulação de canetas emagrecedoras"
      - term: United Arab Emirates
      - definition:
        - text: In the UAE, the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) announced on 1 June 2026 that it had approved oral Wegovy (semaglutide) for long-term weight management in adults with obesity, or overweight with weight-related conditions, and a Ministry of Health and Prevention alert (Circular 9217/2024, October 2024) described genuine Mounjaro as registered for type 2 diabetes and weight management. Federal Decree-Law 38/2024 bars compounding pharmacies from compounding essential copies of products that hold an EDE marketing approval unless no commercially available product can deliver the expected benefit to the patient. On 20 July 2026 the EDE warned that 1,659 packs of Mounjaro and Ozempic missing from a warehouse are outside the legitimate supply chain and told the public to buy these medicines only from licensed pharmacies.
        - generic: "Source: Emirates Drug Establishment approves oral Wegovy® (semaglutide) for weight management and cardiovascular risk reduction · MOHAP Circular No. (9217)/2024: Alert Against the use of Counterfeit version of medicinal product (Mounjaro) · Federal Decree-Law No. (38) of 2024 Governing Medical Products, Pharmacists and Pharmaceutical Establishments (official English translation) · EDE Circular No. (31/2026): Awareness Circular – Stolen Packs of Mounjaro® and Ozempic®"
      - term: Saudi Arabia
      - definition:
        - text: Saudi product information describes weight-management or diabetes indications, depending on brand. These are not skin-rejuvenation approvals. Sudden visual symptoms require urgent ophthalmological assessment. Current Saudi product-record and label verification for Mounjaro (tirzepatide) remains open in this edition; this does not mean it is banned or unregistered.
        - generic: "Source: SFDA-agreed semaglutide safety communication and Saudi indications"
    - paragraph: The facial changes in this lesson happen to people taking approved drugs for approved reasons. Know the indications, and their dates, before you discuss the side effects. Status below is for the US, from FDA records checked in September 2026.
    - strong: Ozempic (semaglutide)
    - generic: Type 2 diabetes
    - generic: First approved 2017. The label adds cardiovascular and kidney risk reduction in people with type 2 diabetes.
    - strong: Wegovy (semaglutide)
    - generic: Chronic weight management
    - generic: Approved June 2021; adolescents from age 12 added December 2022. Cardiovascular risk reduction in established heart disease with obesity or overweight, March 2024. MASH with moderate to advanced liver fibrosis, accelerated approval, August 2025.
    - strong: Mounjaro (tirzepatide)
    - generic: Type 2 diabetes
    - generic: First approved 2022. The label adds cardiovascular risk reduction in type 2 diabetes at high risk.
    - strong: Zepbound (tirzepatide)
    - generic: Chronic weight management
    - generic: Approved November 2023. Moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnoea with obesity, December 2024.
    - strong: Compounded, counterfeit or 'research' versions
    - generic: Not FDA-approved
    - generic: FDA warns about compounded, counterfeit and falsely labelled 'research' semaglutide and tirzepatide (page current 1 September 2026). Semaglutide bought online without a prescription has failed independent testing.
    - paragraph: Approved for diabetes, weight, the heart, the liver and sleep apnoea. The face is on none of these labels.
